newsitem.title: USA: FPL EXPECTS SALES GROWTH TO CONTINUE.
newsitem.headline: FPL EXPECTS SALES GROWTH TO CONTINUE.

text.p: FPL Group Inc expects its sales growth to continue through all of 1997, Chief Financial Analyst Michael Yackira said Tuesday.
In remarks prepared for an analysts' meeting, he said "customer accounts should increase at about the rate we've experienced in the past few years, which is just under 2 percent annually."
So far this year, Florida Power & Light Co President Paul Evanson said, new customer growth has been at an annual rate of 1.8 percent.

"If sales are higher," Yackira pointed out, "the earnings impact would be partially offset by higher sales-related depreciation." Under the company's accelerated depreciation, he explained, depreciation increases as sales rise.
He noted second quarter earnings were up 9 percent to 164 million on a 4 percent increase in kilowatt hour sales on warmer weather and customer growth. Depreciation increased by about $25 million.
He said "The third quater started with very warm weather."
"Operation and maintenance per kilowatt-hour should be lower for the full year 1997 as compared to 1996, as was the case in each of the past six years," Yackira said.
For the 12 months ended June 30, Evanson said, O&M costs declined to $0.012 per kilowatt hour.
Yackira said interst and preferred diviendswill be lower this year, reflecting continuing actions to reduce dept and preferred stock.
He said the payoff of $150 million of debentures that matured July 1 will add about $0.03 to annual per share earnings.
Evanson said the second half replacement of the St. Lucie nuclear unit #1 steam generator is budgeted at $100 million .
